subject.title: fix(gateway): bound SQLite title field reads for sessions.list

question: Should SQLite-backed sessions intentionally adopt the file-backed 8192-byte title-discovery limit, even when an existing SQLite transcript previously derived a title from a later first user message?
rationale: The branch deliberately trades a previously broader SQLite title search for file-path parity and bounded work; code review can verify the implementation, but cannot choose the intended upgrade semantics for existing users.

options.title: Adopt file-path parity
options.body: After fixing the SQL-side allocation bound, accept the 8192-byte title-discovery limit for SQLite sessions and document it as the shared transcript contract.

options.title: Preserve prior SQLite discovery
options.body: Keep a bounded indexed or projection-backed way to locate the first usable user message so upgrades retain SQLite title derivation beyond the head window.

recommendation.title: Adopt file-path parity
recommendation.body: After fixing the SQL-side allocation bound, accept the 8192-byte title-discovery limit for SQLite sessions and document it as the shared transcript contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The only directly evidenced person connected to the reviewed design and current implementation is the contributor who authored the revised head-budget approach; confidence is low because current-main feature-history ownership was unavailable in the supplied context.
